transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Reyes (NimbleSight Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (Infra Lead), Priya Menon (Data Security)

SUMMARY (auto): Walkthrough of model catalog synthesis, selecting open models for Nimblesight use cases, benchmark plan, and routing/playbook recommendations for latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive endpoints. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot bench and share security docs.

TOPICS: model shortlisting, benchmark matrix, quantization tradeoffs, routing policies, VPC/proxying, compliance docs

ACTION ITEMS: See metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya, i'll run the demo today with r ravi on the tech side
[00:06] Olivia Reyes: hey thanks, Olivia here. excited to see how you map open models to our workload
[00:10] Ravi Patel: hey all, i'll jump into the runtime and the catalog shortly. quick ask before we start, what's the primary metric — p95 latency or token cost per infer?
[00:20] Ethan Brooks: p95 for real time features, cost second. we have a couple of batch jobs that can be slower.
[00:25] Priya Menon: and from security, we need keys in our KMS, SOC2 attestation, and audit log retention for 13 months. also SSO via SAML.
[00:35] Maya Chen: that's great, we support SSO/SAML and KMS integrations for Private. SOC2 is in our compliance pack — i'll share the link. for the demo, we'll start with catalog shortlisting and then show a bench plan and routing playbook.
[00:48] Ravi Patel: opening the console — apologies if the screen share stutters — so the catalog view shows models grouped by family, quantization, and runtime-fit. notice the right column 'compatibility matrix' — it has hardware rows (A100, H100, low-memory t4-like) and columns for perf signals.
[01:10] Olivia Reyes: i see. can you show how you score models for our prompt set? we care about code generation and summarization fidelity.
[01:18] Ravi Patel: yes, we have curated benchmark buckets. you can upload a prompt set or pick from templates — we're looking at rouge/bleu proxies plus subjective caliper. for code we use execution-based tests where possible — we run small compile-and-run tests in a sandboxed harness.
[01:34] Maya Chen: i'll add that NimbleSight can set weights per task — for example weight accuracy 0.7, latency 0.3. the catalog then re-sorts automatically.
[01:42] Ethan Brooks: about quantization — how aggressive do you go? we've seen hallucination spike with 4-bit on some models.
[01:50] Ravi Patel: totally. our optimize engine recommends profiles: 'safety-first' (fp16), 'cost-saver' (int8 q4), and 'balanced' (q4f16 hybrid). we also show delta in eval scores — but yes, for code tasks we often avoid 4-bit unless the bench shows parity.
[02:06] Priya Menon: for Private deployment, do you support bringing our own HSM-backed KMS?
[02:12] Maya Chen: yes, BYOK with HSM is supported — we'll need your key policy and we'll map it in the control plane. audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[02:20] Olivia Reyes: can you walk through routing? our plan is to have a low-latency path for chat and a cost path for nightly summarization.
[02:28] Ravi Patel: routing policies are policy-as-code. you can set rules like: if user_tier==premium AND seq_len<512 route to low-latency model var; else route to cost-optimized variant. we also support region, capacity-tier fallbacks and can route based on live perf signals.
[02:46] Maya Chen: and we have automatic fallback to smaller models when dedicated capacity is saturated — reduces p99 spikes.
[02:53] Ethan Brooks: what about A/B and canary? we run canaries on new model versions.
[02:58] Ravi Patel: yes, built-in canary and gradual rollout with traffic split, and automatic rollback if error rate or latency thresholds are breached.
[03:10] Olivia Reyes: can we integrate our internal model blacklist? we have a few models with licensing issues.
[03:15] Maya Chen: absolutely. the catalog supports allow/deny lists per account and per team.
[03:20] Ethan Brooks: benchmarks — what’s included in the bench matrix? we need to compare throughput, p95, token/sec, and memory footprint on both H100 and A100.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: bench matrix includes p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, memory working set, and cost per 1M tokens at current pricing. you can run bench on our hosted infra or we can ship a runner for your private deployment.
[03:45] Olivia Reyes: we might start on hosted to iterate then move to a private VPC pilot. how do you handle networking egress and data residency?
[03:52] Maya Chen: for private we do VPC peering or PrivateLink style connections; logs and data stay in your VPC for Private deployments. hosted API keeps no customer data beyond the request window unless you opt into retention for fine-tuning — this is opt-in.
[04:10] Ethan Brooks: how accurate are the cost estimates? we need forecasting for commit sizing.
[04:14] Ravi Patel: estimates use observed tokens/sec across models + your traffic profile to project monthly cost; we can export CSVs and scenario projections.
[04:24] Olivia Reyes: show us an example shortlist for a summarization workflow — what models would you recommend?
[04:30] Ravi Patel: sure, let me filter to summarization templates and medium-length seqs. demo: shortlist shows three candidates: Open-Large-v2 (fp16), Redwood-Light-q4 (q4f16), and Community-7B-quant. Compatibility matrix flags Community-7B as memory-light but lower ROUGE in our bench by ~5 points.
[04:55] Maya Chen: we often recommend a two-variant routing: default to Redwood-Light-q4 for cost, and for premium route to Open-Large-v2. canary new models against holdout prompts.
[05:05] Priya Menon: about logging — can you redact PII before logs leave our network?
[05:10] Ravi Patel: we provide pre-send scrubbing hooks and onboard text redaction pipelines. with Private you can run that inside your VPC.
[05:20] Olivia Reyes: any recommended guardrails for code generation? licensing and exec safety?
[05:24] Maya Chen: we add prompt-level filters, execution sandboxes for code runouts, and license metadata in the catalog so you can block models with incompatible licenses.
[05:34] Ethan Brooks: what's the bench cadence? if we run weekly benches will you track regressions?
[05:38] Ravi Patel: yes, Optimize monitors quality signals against anchor prompt sets and fires regression alerts with sample diffs.
[05:46] Maya Chen: to move forward i'd propose a 2-week pilot: you provide prompt set and traffic profile; we run bench on hosted and return a matrix + routing playbook.
[05:55] Olivia Reyes: that sounds good. timeline-wise we want pilot results before our December planning session.
[06:00] Maya Chen: we can target initial bench by Nov 23rd. r ravi will set up the runner and maya will send pricing.
[06:08] Ethan Brooks: about private deployment — hardware reqs? we have mixed cluster but can provision h100 if needed.
[06:14] Ravi Patel: minimum for our recommended Open-Large-v2 is 80GB GPU mem for stable perf; Redwood-Light can run on 40GB with quantization.
[06:24] Olivia Reyes: competitor question — other vendors promise 'zero config' quantization, should we be skeptical?
[06:30] Maya Chen: yes; zero-config often hides accuracy tradeoffs. we quantify that in the bench and show per-prompt drift.
[06:38] Priya Menon: please send SOC2 docs and details on retention encryption at rest for logs.
[06:42] Maya Chen: will do, i'll include link to compliance pack and our HSM/BYOK guide.
[06:48] Ravi Patel: demo wrap — i pushed a sample bench run into the console; you can see row-level metrics and export options. i'll also share the bench-runner quickstart in the follow-up.
[06:58] Maya Chen: recap — next steps: send pricing + pilot plan, schedule hands-on bench, customer shares prompts and traffic; agreed target initial bench results by 2027-11-23. any final Qs?
[07:10] Olivia Reyes: none from me, thanks.
[07:14] Ethan Brooks: all good.
[07:16] Priya Menon: thanks, please cc our security contact in the doc share.
[07:20] Maya Chen: will do — thanks everyone.

END

Notes: Transcript has a few mis-heard terms (K-V cache transcribed sometimes as 'k v cask', Redwood Optimize noted as 'Red wood optimize' in one clip). There was minor crosstalk during the runtime demo.
